title: Geometric Entropy and Retrieval Phase Transitions in Continuous Thermal Dense Associative Memory
claim: Phase boundaries show that the kernel choice qualitatively changes where retrieval fails: one has a critical line at every load, the other has a threshold below which retrieval is perfect.
layout: 2 side-by-side phase diagrams, shared axes, dashed threshold line in right panel
description: Two square phase diagrams sit side by side. Both have load alpha = ln(p)/N on the x-axis (0 to 0.6) and temperature T on the y-axis (0 to 2.5). Each is split into a blue Retrieval region and a red Non-retrieval region, with white bold labels. In the left panel a thick black critical curve drops steeply from high T near alpha≈0.02 to a black dot at (0.5, 0). A dotted vertical line marks alpha=0.5. In the right panel the blue region fills everything left of a dashed vertical line at alpha=0.25, marked by a small square at the bottom. A black dot at that line, labeled T_max = 0.22, starts a short curve that falls to a dot at (0.5, 0). The eye goes first to the strong blue/red contrast and the black curves.
caption: Phase diagrams for spherical DAM with exponential capacity M = eαN. Left: LSE kernel. The critical line αc(T ) (solid black) separates retrieval (blue) from non-retrieval at all loads. Right: LSR kernel with b = 3.41. Below the support threshold αth = 0.25 (dashed line), no critical line exists and retrieval is perfect at any temperature. Above threshold, the critical line αc(T ) bounds the retrieval region, reaching Tmax ≈0.22 at α = αth. Both kernels achieve αc(0) = 0.5 at zero temperature (dotted line).
abstract: We study the thermodynamic memory capacity of modern Hopfield networks (Dense Associative Memory models) with continuous states under geometric constraints, extending classical analyses of pairwise associative memory. We derive thermodynamic phase boundaries for Dense Associative Memory networks with exponential capacity $M = e^{Î±N}$, comparing Gaussian (LSE) and Epanechnikov (LSR) kernels. For continuous neurons on an $N$-sphere, the geometric entropy depends solely on the spherical geometry, not the kernel. In the sharp-kernel regime, the maximum theoretical capacity $Î±= 0.5$ is achieved at zero temperature; below this threshold, a critical line separates retrieval from non-retrieval. The two kernels differ qualitatively in their phase boundary structure: for LSE, a critical line exists at all loads $Î±> 0$. For LSR, the finite support introduces a threshold $Î±_{\text{th}}$ below which no spurious patterns contribute to the noise floor, and no critical line exists -- retrieval is perfect at any temperature. These results advance the theory of high-capacity associative memory and clarify fundamental limits of retrieval robustness in modern attention-like memory architectures.
